audit.whatIsWrong: Levels 3, 4-5 and 2+ items were scored Skill while whys[2], whys[3] and whys[6] all describe Sylas winning them outright ('never duel him').
audit.why: The packet chart reads Sylas from level 3 onward and the matchup win rate is 37.5% — the tokens were the only part of the page claiming this is even.
audit.corrected: Rows 2, 3 and 6 proposed as matched full+content pairs to Sylas, ratings dropped, and the three template whys rewritten to say why.

audit.whatIsWrong: Hijack was described as a threat with no cooldown attached, so the reader has no idea how often the steal comes back.
audit.why: Hijack is 80/55/30s — at rank 3 he re-steals an ultimate every 30 seconds, which is why 'don't ult near him' is a permanent rule rather than a one-time caution.
audit.corrected: Real numbers added to whys[4], spikes[2] and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two systematic errors. The page calls his heal 'Q/W drain' or 'Q/W lifesteal' in six places — Chain Lash (Q) has no healing at all; Kingslayer (W) is the heal, on a cooldown that falls from 12s to 6s. And it calls E a 'chain-dash stun' in seven places, when Riot's text describes Abscond as a dash whose recast, Abduct, throws chains and pulls Sylas to an enemy hit. No CC appears in that text.
audit.why: If you think the Q heals him you play around the wrong button; if you think the E stuns you assume you are dead on contact rather than still able to keep hopping. The real threat is that one button is two 400-unit gap-closes.
audit.corrected: Every 'Q/W drain' rewritten to Kingslayer, every 'chain-dash stun' rewritten to Abscond into Abduct as a gap-close, plus Chain Lash's slow-then-delayed-explosion added to early.

audit.why: report[8] already calls for early anti-heal, which is the right call against Kingslayer. late now states plainly that without Grievous Wounds his healing simply erases your burn.

edits.after: Your only real window: layer Q sweetspots and the E slow to chip him before Abscond and Kingslayer come fully online.

edits.after: Hijack steals your Lilting Lullaby — he can sleep YOU and your team, and it is back every 30s late, so never ult near him.

edits.before: His Q/W lifesteal scales with AP and out-sustains your DoT, while one E stun deletes the kite war you depend on.
edits.after: Kingslayer's heal scales with AP and out-sustains your DoT, while one Abduct ends the kite war you depend on.

edits.before: Sylas is one of the few melee bruisers you cannot just kite to death — his Q/W drain heals back every tick of your Dream Dust burn, so the DoT war you usually win goes nowhere. At levels 1-2 you can poke with the tip of your Q from range while he only has one ability, but the moment he hits 3 his E chain-dash closes the gap and stuns you out of your hops. Do not E into him hoping the slow holds — he just dashes through it. Last-hit with Q and respect that his all-in is real here.
edits.after: Sylas is one of the few melee bruisers you cannot simply kite to death — Kingslayer (W) heals him against champions on a cooldown that falls to 6s, so the DoT war you usually win goes nowhere. At levels 1-2 you can poke with the tip of your Q while he has one ability, but from 3 Abscond and its Abduct recast close the gap in two hops. Watch Chain Lash as well: it slows where the chains cross and explodes there a moment later, so the ground he aims at is the ground to leave. Last-hit with Q; his all-in is real.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 are where this lane turns sour. Your Q is maxed and the burn compounds, but his drain sustains through it while his E stun catches you the instant your movement-speed buffer drops. At 6 the trap is his R: it STEALS your Lilting Lullaby, so if you ult to set up a sleep he takes it and sleeps you instead — keep your R holstered in lane unless your jungler is collapsing. Bait the E chain-dash on a Q escape and only step up while it is down; that is your one safe trade pattern.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 are where this lane turns sour. Your Q is maxed and the burn compounds, but Kingslayer sustains through it while Abduct hauls him onto you the instant your move-speed buffer drops. At 6 the trap is Hijack: it STEALS your Lilting Lullaby, so ulting to set up a sleep just hands him one — and late he gets another steal every 30 seconds. Keep your R holstered unless your jungler is collapsing. Bait Abscond on a Q escape and step up only during its 13s downtime; that is your one safe pattern.

edits.before: This stays his lane into items. His Q/W lifesteal scales with AP and out-sustains your W and DoT in any extended fight, and a single E stun isolates you — you are squishy with no defensive button, so one chain-dash lands and you are deleted. Do not try to 1v1 a fed Sylas. Your value is sidelane pressure and picking the burn-and-roam onto squishier targets; force the map elsewhere and let your team body-block his all-in rather than feeding him a stolen ult.
edits.after: This stays his lane into items. Kingslayer's heal scales with AP and out-sustains your W and DoT in any long fight, and Abscond into Abduct crosses two 400-unit hops onto a squishy with no defensive button. Do not 1v1 a fed Sylas. Grievous Wounds is the item that changes the maths — without it his healing simply erases your burn. Your value is sidelane pressure and burn-and-roam onto softer targets; force the map elsewhere and let your team body-block rather than feeding him a stolen ult.

notes: I deliberately did NOT keep the claim that Sylas's E stuns. Riot's Abduct text describes only a chain-throw that pulls him to the target — no CC — so I restated it as a gap-close rather than assert or deny a stun. If the user knows Abduct applies CC in-game, the seven strings I rewrote are where to add it back; it is listed in unverified.
